text:
Wrecked, anchored, I took out again

the yellow notebook

I write from bed

as I did last

year.


I am going to the doctor

on Monday.

‘Yes, doctor, weak legs, dizziness,

headache and back

pain.’


‘Do you drink?’ he will ask me.

‘Do you do the exercises,

take the vitamins?’

I think I am simply sick

of life, always the same

stale fluctuating

factors.


Even at the racetrack

I watch the horses run

and it seems to me

that there is no point.


I leave right after betting

on the remaining races.

‘Are you leaving?’ the

clerk will ask me.

‘Yes, it is boring,’

I answer.


‘Look, if you think it is boring

out there,’ he tells me,

‘imagine in here.’


So here I am

propped up again on

the pillows.

Nothing but an old man

just an old writer

with a yellow

notebook.


Something is

coming across the

floor

toward me.


Ah, it is only my cat.

This time.—

translation.title: Wrecked, Anchored, I Took Out Again...
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version attributed to Charles Bukowski. The closing ‘Algo sé / acerca por él / suelo / hacia mí’ contains two contextually clear stray accents; reading them as ‘Algo se / acerca por el / suelo / hacia mí’ yields ‘Something is coming across the floor toward me,’ confirmed by the following identification of the cat.
